name: Core AI vocabulary, Spanish
summary: Spanish terms of both tiers that the English core glossary (core.json) does not match. It applies only to filings whose language is es, together with core.json, which matches the English terms these filings use unchanged (AI, machine learning, ChatGPT, deepfake, big data). Tier `ai` terms denote AI by themselves; tier `context` terms are stand-ins for AI and the wording around which it is discussed (analítica avanzada, sistemas inteligentes, tratamiento automatizado, toma de decisiones basada en datos), and terms that often mean something else in Spanish reports (agente autónomo, caja negra, phrases with modelo). Built by going through the entries of core.json group by group: a term was added, with the tier and group of its English counterpart, where a Spanish wording was found in the official Spanish text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and other EU acts, in IATE, in publications of AEPD, AESIA, CNMV, Banco de España and INCIBE, in annual reports of IBEX 35 companies, in the Spanish-language sample reports in gs://airo-eu-sample-reports or in the Spanish business press; entries for which no Spanish wording was found there are left to core.json. Spanish-specific terms without an English counterpart are included (AESIA, Carta de Derechos Digitales, tratamiento automatizado, modelos analíticos). Inflected forms (plural, gender) and unaccented spellings are listed as variants, because the plural suffix that glossary.py adds is the English one; abbreviations (IA, AESIA, ENIA, RIA, EIPD, CPD, ALIA) are case-sensitive. Status: hit contexts of the tier `ai` terms were checked on the seven Spanish sample reports and on IBEX 35 annual reports; hits and misses were then checked block by block on the 30 Spanish reports of the sector sample (gs://airo-eu-sample-reports/sector-sample), after which variants that only matched non-AI text there were removed and wordings found there were added; to be checked by a native speaker.
